chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Friendship with Sinatra; Al Rinker; refusing a writer
summary: Norvo calls Sinatra honest and sincere, recalls Mildred discovering Al Rinker, and says he refused to talk to a writer fishing for gossip.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: I'm -- I've known him from the beginning you see Mildred's brother, Al Rinker, lived up in Nyack, up in on the other side of the River and we just used to visit him a couple of times and we stopped by when he was working at the

Log Cabin, and Mildred picked him -- the first night, she said "That kid can sing, that kid's going to sing. That young man." So, later, he went with -- he was with somebody, I forget, so we needed somebody to sing extra turns with Mildred.
And I called him, and he just went with Harry James. He just accepted a job with Harry James. And,
Yeah, he just accepted a job with Harry.
OH, yeah. He was with Harry James before he went with Tommy.
And Harry was in the Lincoln Hotel at the time.
And Mildred really thought he was something.
I think it was mutual, too, because --
Oh, I know it had to be.
-- but I always found him very honest and -- and very sincere about these things. To me --
I can't say anything for anybody else --
I just know that our relationship was very, very fine --
-- and he treated us very good, the boys -- the band, he treated us wonderful.
Did he? Duke was fond of him.
Duke was fond of him, Duke -- you know they had a nice relationship. Duke thought a lot of him, too.
I think if -- I think he's a man, if you're straight and Frank, (unintelligible), he knows that I don't mince and I won't say anything wrong --

-- ah -- and I broke up with a writer friend of mine, a very dear friend, but he called me and I know he couldn't get an interview, I sensed it. He was calling me in Vegas and we just got back, and Frank had left us in the Lounge in Vegas, I went down to do a show in Miami with Elvis Presley, after Presley got out --

-- he did a TV show down there. So he called me and I knew that he wasn't -- but, oh no, so we ended I said, "I know why you're calling me and I would never think of doing such a thing. I wouldn't evade his -- if he says at all -- "
He wanted you to talk, huh?
-- I said, "You're baiting me and you're just -- it's just wrong."
And I saw very little of him after that and we had been pretty good friends before. So, I felt I was honest --
-- and if that's all it meant to him, then --
